page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 32-core AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled, it supplies 64 virtual CPUs alongside 128 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Managed via the KVM hypervisor, the instance includes L1d, L2, and L3 cache sizes of 32 KB, 0.5 MB, and 32 MB respectively. Instruction set extensions include AES, VAES, SHA_NI, FMA, and standard AVX, whereas AVX-512 features are not available. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 16 Gbps, and no local ephemeral storage is attached.

Performance benchmarks show strong multi-core computation and throughput characteristics. The instance lands in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations, PassMark CPU tests, extended instruction sets, and hardware encryption benchmarks. Database operations in PassMark and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also score in the upper quartile, alongside a throughput of 61.81 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. In Geekbench testing, ray tracing and image processing perform in the top quartile, while general software compilation with Clang and text processing fall into average performance bands. Small-model LLM prompt processing and text generation remain strong, though medium 7B model execution sits in the average range.

The 1:2 memory ratio provides high compute density for parallel workloads without the added expense of superfluous RAM or dedicated GPU hardware. Tradeoffs include a reliance on network-attached storage due to zero local storage, average large-block uncached memory bandwidth performance, and the absence of AVX-512 execution units. The ecs.c7a.16xlarge instance is suited for multi-threaded batch processing, Redis key-value caching, software compilation, cryptographic processing, and backend database workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 instance running on a dedicated 32-core AMD EPYC 7T83 processor at 2.55 GHz. Configured with 64 vCPUs, 128 GB of memory, and 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, it maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without local ephemeral storage or integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-quartile results in stress-ng multi-core testing, PassMark CPU and encryption benchmarks, PassMark database operations, and Redis SET processing at 61.81 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks and Geekbench multi-core scores remain average. Without local disk storage or AVX-512 support, the instance provides cost-efficient compute density for CPU-heavy applications. It is suited for multi-threaded batch processing, in-memory caching, software compilation, cryptographic services, and backend database tasks.
